messages:
anya: Heads up — I saw a noticeable spike in interactive session failures in us-west1 overnight. Around 18:30 UTC the spot pool got reclaimed and ~20% of active sessions hit error pages :grimacing: 
chao: ugh. any correlation with batch drain / autoscaler events?
anya: yes — batch autoscaler pushed a large job set which saturated the spot pool, then preemptions cascaded. We fell back to on-demand but the route config had an aggressive timeout so sessions dropped.
jamal: do we have a timeline? metrics?
anya: logs: infra-bot posted an event at 1862001400 about mass preemptions. I pulled the pod restarts and it lines up. Preemption rate jumped from 0.6% -> 7% in a 10m window.
infra-bot: [incident] detected: spot-preemptions/us-west1 increased by 10x between 1862001300 and 1862001400. Affected nodepool: gpu-spot-rt-32.
mike: rough cost tradeoff numbers here? how much are we saving with current spot ratio vs the cost of these failures?
lena: rough calc — last month spot mix saved ~62% on GPU bill, but user-facing error cost (support + retention risk) is hard to quantify. For this outage, estimated 400 failed interactive requests, ~3% of active user sessions at peak.
chao: a few quick mitigation ideas: 1) short-term: increase on-demand buffer for interactive routing to 10% capacity and bump route timeouts; 2) medium: add preemption-safety labels and use eviction-priority for batch; 3) longer: predictive hedging for high-risk windows.
anya: +1. Also we should throttle large batch floods during off-peak bursts — they can be scheduled into off-peak but they were submitted as 'now' and autoscaler happily spun up spot nodes.
jamal: Could we add an interactive-only reservation / warm pool? e.g., keep 6 on-demand GPUs per region pinned to interactive queue. That would reduce preemption exposure.
mike: yes but cost goes up. What if we implement a tiny warm pool and an emergency fast-fallback that migrates sessions to smaller quantized model instances (cheaper) during preemptions? That preserves UX at lower perf.
lena: that seems promising — fallback to ord-quant small model for reads + short completions. Need to ensure model routing supports rapid fallback.
ops-runner: pinging scheduler team. We can implement a new priority rule in the queue scheduler to mark 'interactive' jobs with higher permanence and add preemption-tolerant flags to batch. Example scheduler override: 
```yaml
queues:
  interactive:
    min_reserved_gpus: 6
    fallback_model: rdm-small-quant
  batch:
    preemptible: true
    max_burst: 120
    eviction_priority: low
```
chao: also, add a cooldown window for scaling down spot nodepools during high preemption rate windows. The autoscaler should be conservative for 15m after a large reclaim event.
anya: for immediate patch I propose: 1) set route timeout from 10s -> 30s for interactive in west, 2) reserve 6 on-demand GPUs in us-west1, 3) add queue scheduler rule to deprioritize batch during peak interactive windows.
mike: approve for emergency change. ops-runner, can you run a canary?
ops-runner: starting canary now. Will cordon / drain logic remain as-is?
jamal: note: cordon/drain must prefer evicting batch pods first. We should add node taints so interactive pods tolerate on-demand-only taints. 
chao: sample taint/toleration: 
```yaml
nodeTaints:
  - key: "reserved-type"
    value: "on-demand"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
podTolerations:
  - key: "reserved-type"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "on-demand"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
```
lena: also watch network egress limits — when we spin fallback small models they still hit the same feature-store endpoints and we saw a transient networking thrash last time. Recommend temporary rate-limiter on feature-store calls per session.
anya: good call. I'll open a quick PR to patch route timeouts and add the on-demand reservation. Jamal, can you own the scheduler rule change?
jamal: yes, will draft the override and start tests.
ops-runner: canary results: small pass. Preemption still occurred but interactive error rate dropped ~85% in canary region.
infra-bot: [metric] interactive-error-rate/us-west1 reduced from 18% -> 2.7% during canary window.
mike: great. Follow-ups: (A) formalize warm-pool + fallback routing (B) run cost simulation for warm pool sizes (C) add autoscaler cooldown heuristic and eviction-priority labels.
anya: i put tasks in the eng-infra board and linked to this thread. For the doc: we should capture tradeoffs — 62% cost savings vs 3% UX defects risk. Recommend we keep spot-heavy batch but isolate interactive with the small warm pool + fallback.
chao: addendum — consider region-aware hedging: if us-west1 preemptions exceed threshold, route new interactive sessions to us-central1 fallback (if latency delta acceptable).
jamal: noted. I'll prototype routing policy by EOD.
lena: will monitor support mentions and usage metrics overnight. Thanks team :thumbsup:
